findings: November is a full overview of Optimized Checkout Suite payments UIs, dynamic payment methods and Link. It retains Payment Links for no-code acceptance without a website, positions a prebuilt full page (embedded or redirected on the merchant website) as recommended, gives a distinct embedded-form route, lists custom Elements and Mobile Payment Element for iOS, Android and React Native, and labels Dashboard Checkout studio Private preview. The April overview covered hosted/embedded Checkout, Elements, Payment Links and iOS/Android and explicitly required Stripe account signup (old raw lines 8–20, new raw lines 5–27).

Both captures prefer Checkout Sessions for most integrations, with November expanding the comparison. Checkout Sessions can use `price_data` for basic collection or line items, address collection, tax, discounts, shipping, subscriptions, order details, dynamic inventory/line-item updates and Adaptive Pricing for fuller flows. `automatic_tax.enabled=true` enables Stripe Tax in the stated example; PaymentIntents offers lower-level control and merchant ownership of final amount and checkout lifecycle, requiring separately integrated tax and subscriptions and merchant-written discounts, shipping, address/order tracking, currency conversion and amount updates. Adaptive Pricing is a Checkout Sessions product feature, not established for PaymentIntents just because currency conversion can be built separately (old raw line 8, new raw lines 29–62).

November's comparison describes Checkout Session expiration at 24 hours and full lifecycle events versus PaymentIntent payment-status events and no automatic Session expiration. The separate November Checkout Sessions create API gives 24-hour default with configurable `expires_at` 30 minutes to 24 hours after creation. The separate Checkout Session object distinguishes `status=complete` with possible payment processing from `payment_status` for fulfillment. No table entry authorizes fulfillment, proves receipt or funding, or describes an exhaustive list of account event types (new raw lines 59–62; related Checkout API create lines 316–317 and object lines 312–322, 368–378; mapped source lines 34–45, 54–62).

November adds consumer/merchant routing topics: dynamic payment methods display/order, scenarios via method configurations, availability rules, Dashboard A/B testing, and a Private preview Checkout studio method-management route. Link can reuse saved credit/debit cards and U.S. bank accounts across Link-enabled businesses and names Instant Bank Payments and Klarna. The overview links Checkout, Web Elements and native iOS/Android/React Native Link. Separate Link docs show Wallet settings and eligible transaction filtering, and business, presentment, amount, customer location, subscription/recurrence restrictions, so the overview does not promise every method displays or succeeds. Shopify, Squarespace and Adobe Commerce are partner/app routes, without implementation or availability detail (new raw lines 64–96; related Link integration lines 7–16 and funding lines 40–52).

New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-online-payments-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-design-payments-integration-2025.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-accept-a-payment.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/online-payments`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/online-payments, the November 7 guide describes the Optimized Checkout Suite’s payment UIs, dynamic payment methods and Link. It names no-code Payment Links without a website, the recommended full-page Checkout experience embedded or redirected on a merchant site, a separate prebuilt embedded form, custom Elements, Mobile Payment Element on iOS, Android and React Native, and Dashboard Checkout studio in Private preview (new raw lines 5-27). The April overview already described Payment Links, hosted and embedded Checkout, Elements, iOS and Android and explicitly required Stripe signup (old raw lines 8-20). Both favor Checkout Sessions for most integrations. November distinguishes basic `price_data` collection and fuller Session-owned checkout with built-in Stripe Tax, shipping, discounts, subscriptions, Adaptive Pricing, address/order tools and dynamic updates from the lower-level PaymentIntent route where the merchant computes the amount and owns checkout logic, integrating Tax and Subscriptions separately as needed. It contrasts default 24-hour Session expiry and checkout lifecycle events with PaymentIntent's lack of automatic Session expiry and payment-state tracking. Session completion is distinct from paid status (new raw lines 29-62, and separate Session object reference lines 312-322 and 368-378). Dynamic payment methods, eligibility rules, configurations and A/B tests are decision tools. Link reuses saved credit/debit cards or U.S. bank accounts and names Instant Bank Payments and Klarna, with separate Checkout/web/mobile routes and eligible transaction conditions. Shopify, Squarespace and Adobe Commerce are discovery routes (new raw lines 64-96). `source-stripe-accept-a-payment.md` currently covers the distinct `/payments/accept-a-payment` index and April implementation and only links this overview's April-dated predecessor at line 90.
reviewed_answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/online-payments, the substantive change is fuller strategy coverage through UI, API and feature comparisons, Private preview Checkout studio, payment method controls, Link and partner routes (old raw lines 8-32 and new raw lines 13-96). Title, layout, demo link and changed quickstart targets are presentation or navigation. Keep the April signup statement, no-code product links and Checkout Sessions client-secret and confirmation example dated (old raw lines 8-32). Their omission does not establish a signup waiver or a product removal. Keep this full November overview distinct from the November 20-line `/payments/accept-a-payment` variant index and April implementation already described by `source-stripe-accept-a-payment.md`. For the UI terminology (new raw lines 17-27 and 39-57), the separate Checkout Form quickstart sends `ui_mode=form`, the full embedded page uses API `ui_mode=embedded_page`, and the separate Accept a Payment index uses `ui=embedded-page` as a URL selector. The `2026-03-25.dahlia` Checkout Session create contract replaces `hosted`, `embedded`, and `custom` with `hosted_page`, `embedded_page`, and `elements`, rejects all three old values on that version, and adds `form` separately (Dahlia changelog lines 9-28). Route the warning reciprocally to `source-stripe-checkout-sessions.md` lines 33-44 and preserve its dated metadata sample’s literal `ui_mode=custom` alongside the warning that it fails on Dahlia. Read the 24-hour Checkout Session expiry as the API default, configurable from 30 minutes to 24 hours, and keep PaymentIntent events distinct (new raw lines 59-62). Qualify `wiki/concepts/stripe-checkout.md` line 27’s embedded return-page `complete` to ‘success’ shorthand reciprocally. `status=complete` can support checkout completion messaging while payment is still processing. For paid-order fulfillment use separate server-side `payment_status=paid` and follow the documented delayed events, including `checkout.session.async_payment_succeeded` and `checkout.session.async_payment_failed` (concept lines 202-214 and Checkout Session object lines 312-322 and 368-378). Mobile, Link, preview and partner links provide discovery within the documented eligibility and rollout scope. Runtime payment success and deployed API/SDK versions remain unverified.
